Models

    Meta ships six model lines. Muse Wonder, Muse Spark, Muse Image, Muse Voice Transcribe, and Segment Anything Model (SAM) are hosted on Meta Model API; Muse Glimmer is open-weight and runs on your own hardware. Muse Spark also has an open-weight release, Muse Spark Open. Pick one by what you're building, then read its section for versions and where to use them.

    Models at a glance

    Use caseModelInputOutputAPI endpoints
    Agentic work, coding, and reasoningMuse Wonder, Muse SparkText, image, video, audio, and PDFTextResponses, Chat Completions, Messages
    Image generation and editingMuse ImageText and imageImageResponses, Image generation
    Speech to textMuse Voice TranscribeAudioText (transcription)Transcribe
    Image and video segmentationSegment Anything ModelText prompt, image, and videoText (geometry)Responses, Media segmentation
    Self-hosted or provider-hosted agentic and coding work; post-trainingMuse Spark OpenText, image, video, and audioTextNone (self-host or a hosted provider)
    Self-hosted inference; supervised fine-tuningMuse GlimmerText and imageTextNone (self-host)
    Availability by country

    Model availability can vary by country. See the Geographic Use Policy for country-specific restrictions.

    Muse Wonder

    Muse Wonder is Meta's most capable model, built for complex software engineering and long-horizon agentic work. It makes and verifies changes across many files in real repositories, and it plans, delegates to sub-agents, calls tools in parallel, and recovers from errors across many steps, following detailed instructions closely. Take on hard coding tasks, build personal and professional agents, and drive a desktop with computer use. Muse Wonder also handles chat completion, image understanding, video and audio understanding, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.

    Muse Wonder takes text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, returns text, has a 1,048,576-token context window, and supports reasoning effort levels from "minimal" to "max".

    Preview

    Muse Wonder is in preview. For more about the model, see the Muse Wonder model page and the Muse Wonder model card(opens in new tab).

    Muse Wonder availability

    Muse Wonder comes in two variants. Muse Wonder is on Model API and in Muse Code. Muse Wonder Full, the higher-capability variant, is available only in Muse Code with a subscription, so setting reasoning effort to "max" on Muse Wonder doesn't select it.

    VariantModel API (pay-as-you-go)Muse Code
    Muse Wonder (muse-wonder-1.0)Available (Standard mode only)Pay-as-you-go and every plan
    Muse Wonder FullNot availablePower Usage and Maximum Usage

    With a subscription, Muse Wonder is available on every plan and Muse Wonder Full on the Power Usage and Maximum Usage plans, each in Standard mode and Contributor mode.

    Muse Wonder and Muse Wonder Full aren't currently available in South Korea, on Model API or in Muse Code.

    In Standard mode, your content — the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back — is not used to train Meta models. Muse Code subscribers can also use Contributor mode, which is on by default: it gives you more usage in exchange for letting Meta use your content to train future Meta models, and you can turn it off at any time in your settings. For Muse Wonder, Contributor mode isn't available on pay-as-you-go. See Pricing and rate limits for rates.

    Muse Spark

    Muse Spark is Meta's model for agentic and coding work, such as multi-step tool loops, software engineering assistants, and long-context reasoning. Use it for chat completion, image understanding, video and audio understanding, tool calling, structured output, and search grounding.

    Muse Spark comes in three versions. All take text, image, video, audio, and PDF input, return text, and have a 1,048,576-token context window. They differ by capability:

    • Muse Spark 1.3 (muse-spark-1.3): the latest version, tuned for agentic workflows (multi-step tool, browser, and long-horizon tasks) with improved coding over 1.2. Supports all reasoning effort levels, including the "max" level for extended reasoning (not available with muse-spark-1.3-contributor). Recommended for new work.
    • Muse Spark 1.2 (muse-spark-1.2): the previous version.
    • Muse Spark 1.1 (muse-spark-1.1): the original version.
    Audio input on Muse Spark 1.3

    Audio understanding in Muse Spark 1.3 is not fully supported, and response quality for requests that include audio may be degraded. For audio, use Muse Spark 1.2, or Muse Voice Transcribe for dedicated speech-to-text.

    muse-spark-1.3 is the default model in most code examples in these docs. The coding agents, agent frameworks, and computer use guides use muse-wonder-1.0 for long-running agentic work.

    Muse Spark availability

    Every Muse Spark version is available on pay-as-you-go. All versions except Muse Spark 1.1 are also available in Muse Code, on pay-as-you-go and with any subscription.

    VersionModel API (pay-as-you-go)Muse Code
    Muse Spark 1.3 (muse-spark-1.3)Standard modePay-as-you-go and every plan
    Muse Spark 1.3 Contributor (muse-spark-1.3-contributor)Contributor modePay-as-you-go and every plan
    Muse Spark 1.2 (muse-spark-1.2)Standard modePay-as-you-go and every plan
    Muse Spark 1.2 Contributor (muse-spark-1.2-contributor)Contributor modePay-as-you-go and every plan
    Muse Spark 1.1 (muse-spark-1.1)Standard modeNot available

    In Standard mode, your content is not used to train Meta models. In Contributor mode, your content may be used to train future Meta models, in exchange for a lower price. On pay-as-you-go, switch between the two by choosing the model ID: for example, muse-spark-1.3 for Standard mode or muse-spark-1.3-contributor for Contributor mode. Muse Spark 1.1 is available in Standard mode only. See Pricing and rate limits for rates.

    Choose Muse Wonder or Muse Spark

    Muse Wonder and Muse Spark take the same requests on the same endpoints, so moving a workload between them is a model ID change. Choose by workload:

    • Muse Wonder: long-running, complex tasks where capability matters more than cost per token, such as multi-file coding changes, multi-hour agent runs, and sub-agent orchestration.
    • Muse Spark: high-volume, latency-sensitive, or cost-sensitive work, such as sub-agent tasks, classification, and tight tool loops. On Model API, Muse Spark also offers a discounted Contributor mode.

    Muse Image

    Muse Image is Meta's image generation model line. Send a text prompt (and optional reference images) and get an image back, or send an image with an instruction to edit it. One model handles both generation and editing. It's agentic, so it can search the web for visual references and current facts and run code to build layouts before it renders.

    Model IDInputOutput
    muse-image-1.0Text, imageImage

    Reach Muse Image two ways: the Responses API for conversational, multi-turn editing, or the single-shot /v1/images/generations and /v1/images/edits endpoints for one-off calls. See the Image generation guide to get started.

    Muse Voice Transcribe

    Muse Voice Transcribe is Meta's speech-to-text model on Meta Model API. Use it to transcribe live audio streams or supported audio files.

    Model IDInputOutput
    muse-voice-transcribe-1.0AudioText transcript

    Muse Voice Transcribe is built for real-time speech products: voice agents, meeting and call intelligence, live transcription, dictation, captioning, and high-volume transcription. It supports streaming speaker diarization, native endpointing and voice activity detection, contextual and keyword biasing, 25 evaluated languages with code-switching, and turn-level timestamps.

    It returns transcript text. It does not synthesize speech or provide a speech-to-speech conversation API. It does not provide word-level timestamps, sound event detection, or emotion detection.

    Reach Muse Voice Transcribe two ways: the realtime WebSocket endpoint (wss://api.meta.ai/v1/asr/realtime) for live audio, or the file endpoint (POST /v1/asr/transcribe) for a recording you already have.

    Start with the Muse Voice Transcribe guide. See Pricing and rate limits for audio pricing.

    Segment Anything Model

    SAM 3.1 is Meta's segmentation model on Meta Model API. Give it a short noun phrase such as "yellow school bus" with an image or video, and it returns every match as a box and a pixel-accurate mask. Or mark specific objects with boxes and points to segment only those objects. One model handles both stills and clips, and in video it follows each object across frames.

    Model IDInputOutput
    sam-3.1Text prompt, image, videoBoxes and masks

    Reach SAM 3.1 over the Responses API (POST /v1/responses), and upload clips through the Files API when you segment them more than once. See the Media segmentation guide to get started.

    Muse Spark Open

    Muse Spark Open is the open-weight release of Muse Spark: an 816B-parameter mixture-of-experts model with 42B active parameters. You don't call it over Model API. Download the weights and serve them through a runtime such as SGLang, vLLM, TensorRT-LLM, or llama.cpp, or call it through a hosted inference provider.

    Muse Spark Open lives in the Open-weight models section:

    • Muse Spark Open overview: checkpoints, hardware, license, and launch partners.
    • Get the model: download the BF16 or NVFP4 weights.
    • Run inference: serve it on your own GPUs or call a hosted provider.
    • Post-training: adapt it with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL).

    Muse Glimmer

    Muse Glimmer is Meta's open-weight multimodal model, distilled from Muse Spark and built to run on your own hardware. You run it yourself instead of calling it over Model API: download the weights and serve them through a runtime such as vLLM, SGLang, llama.cpp, or ExecuTorch.

    Muse Glimmer lives in the Open-weight models section, covering how to get, prompt, deploy, and customize the model:

    • Muse Glimmer overview: variants, architecture, license, and launch partners.
    • Get the model: download the weights and verify your setup.
    • Run inference: pick a runtime and serve it locally.
    • Post-training: adapt it to your domain with supervised fine-tuning (SFT) or reinforcement learning (RL).

    List models via the API

    Query the catalog programmatically when you need to check what's enabled for your team. This returns the API-hosted models; self-hosted Muse Glimmer isn't included.

    ←→to navigate

    The response returns models sorted newest-first by creation time, with the model ID as a stable tiebreaker. Each object includes a created field — the Unix timestamp in seconds for when the model was added to the registry. GET /v1/models/{model} returns the same created value for a single model.

    See also

    • Pricing and rate limits: per-token rates for Standard and Contributor mode, and rate limits for each model
    • Subscriptions: Muse Code plans and what each one includes
    On this page

      Please confirm your identity

      For added security, you need to confirm your identity. You will be taken to your single sign-on provider, where you can enter your password.

Pricing and rate limits

    Use our models with pay-as-you-go billing on Meta Model API and in Muse Code, or in Muse Code with a monthly subscription. This page covers pay-as-you-go: Model API bills text models per token, image generation per image, Muse Voice Transcribe by the hour of audio processed, and Segment Anything Model (SAM) per image or video frame segmented, with no minimums or upfront commitment.

    Pricing modes

    Some models can be used in two modes. Standard mode uses standard pricing. Contributor mode offers discounted pricing or more usage in exchange for permission to use your content — the prompts, code, files, and context you send, plus the model responses you get back — to train future Meta models.

    Standard mode

    In Standard mode, you pay standard prices and your content is not used to train Meta models. Every model on this page is available in Standard mode.

    Contributor mode

    On Model API, Contributor mode runs the same models at heavily discounted token prices, in exchange for permission to use your content to train future Meta models. It lowers the barrier to entry for prototyping, testing integrations, and scaling experiments where it's acceptable for Meta to use your content to train future Meta models.

    On Model API, use Contributor mode with Muse Spark 1.3 or 1.2 by calling its Contributor-mode variant: muse-spark-1.3-contributor or muse-spark-1.2-contributor. Contributor mode isn't available for Muse Wonder on Model API.

    In Muse Code, subscriptions default to Contributor mode, and you can turn it on or off in settings; see Contributor mode in Muse Code.

    Model pricing

    Muse Wonder

    Model: muse-wonder-1.0.

    UsageStandard mode (per 1M tokens)Contributor mode (per 1M tokens)
    Cached input$0.20Not available
    Input$4.00Not available
    Output$20.00Not available

    Muse Spark

    Models: muse-spark-1.3, muse-spark-1.2, and muse-spark-1.1 in Standard mode; muse-spark-1.3-contributor and muse-spark-1.2-contributor in Contributor mode. Muse Spark 1.1 is Standard mode only.

    UsageStandard mode (per 1M tokens)Contributor mode (per 1M tokens)
    Cached input$0.15$0.002
    Input$1.25$0.10
    Output$4.25$0.20

    Token pricing notes

    These apply to the token-priced models above, Muse Wonder and Muse Spark.

    • Cached input costs less: When part of your prompt matches a cached prefix, you pay the cached-input rate for those tokens. Check cached_tokens in the response to see how many were served from cache.
    • No long-context premium: you pay the same rate whether your context window is mostly empty or almost full.
    • Web search grounding: $2.50 per 1,000 search queries, in addition to the request's token cost. This applies to the web_search tool on text models such as Muse Wonder and Muse Spark.
    Muse Image search is included

    Muse Image's built-in web and image search is part of its per-image price and isn't charged separately. See Muse Image pricing.

    Muse Image

    UsagePrice
    Generated image$0.01 per image

    Muse Image is billed at a flat rate per generated image. The price is the same regardless of prompt length, reasoning_strength, or the tools the model uses during generation, including its built-in web and image search, which isn't charged separately. A request that returns n images is billed for n images. You're billed only for images the model successfully generates and returns: images that fail to generate, or that are removed by safety filtering before they're returned, aren't counted. Image responses still include a usage object with token counts for reference, but image generation tokens are not included in token-based pricing for other models. See the Image generation guide for the response shape.

    Muse Voice Transcribe

    Muse Voice Transcribe is billed by audio processed, metered in whole seconds.

    UsagePrice
    Audio processed$0.18 per hour

    Streaming and non-streaming transcription are priced the same. Zero data retention (ZDR) is priced at parity with Standard mode. Contributor mode isn't available for Muse Voice Transcribe. Audio time is billed as a separate line item from token usage, rounded down to whole seconds; other endpoints aren't billed for audio time.

    Segment Anything Model 3.1

    SAM 3.1 segmentation is billed per image and per video frame, not per token. The same prices apply to streaming and non-streaming requests. Each video request is billed for at least 50 frames, so a clip or tracking range shorter than 50 frames is billed as 50. The response's usage.video_frames_processed reports the frames billed for that request.

    UsagePrice
    Image segmentation$2.50 per 1,000 images
    Video segmentation$0.20 per 1,000 frames

    Rate limits

    Rate limits apply per team, not per API key: requests, tokens, and streams from every key in a team count toward the same limits. Each model below has its own limits, so traffic to one model doesn't use up another's.

    ModelRequests per minute (RPM)Tokens per minute (TPM)Other limits
    muse-wonder-1.03,0004,000,000
    muse-spark-1.33,0004,000,000
    muse-spark-1.23,0004,000,000
    muse-spark-1.3-contributor1503,000,000
    muse-spark-1.2-contributor1503,000,000
    muse-spark-1.13,0004,000,000
    sam-3.13,000None
    muse-image-1.0150None
    muse-voice-transcribe-1.0NoneNone256 concurrent streams; 16,000 streams per hour

    SAM 3.1 is billed per image or frame and Muse Image is priced per image, so neither has a TPM limit.

    Muse Voice Transcribe is billed by audio processed, so it's limited by streams rather than requests or tokens. Concurrent streams caps how many transcription sessions you hold open at once; streams per hour caps how many you start. Realtime and file transcription share the same budget.

    Token usage counts only your input and output tokens. Meta injects a small amount of steering context into every prompt (a system prompt and related scaffolding); those injected tokens are not billed and are excluded from the token counts reported in your usage and by the token-counting endpoints.

    Background responses

    Creating background responses (background: true) is limited to 600 submissions per minute, per team, in addition to the limits above. The cap applies only to starting new background responses: over it, new submissions return HTTP 429 Too Many Requests with a Retry-After header, and responses already running continue unaffected.

    Handle rate limits

    When you exceed a limit, the API rejects the request. Requests succeed again once usage drops below the limit.

    Retry on 429 responses

    Retry strategy: Use exponential backoff with jitter. Start with a short delay such as 500 ms, double it after each consecutive rate-limit response, and add random jitter so concurrent clients don't all retry at the same moment. If the response includes a Retry-After header, wait at least that long.

    Read rate-limit headers

    Every successful token-based response includes headers that report your current limit and remaining quota:

    HeaderDescription
    x-ratelimit-limit-tokensTotal token budget for the current window.
    x-ratelimit-remaining-tokensTokens remaining before you hit the limit.
    x-ratelimit-limit-requestsTotal request budget for the current window.
    x-ratelimit-remaining-requestsRequests remaining before you hit the limit.

    Read these headers and slow down before you hit a rate limit instead of reacting after one.

    Handle Muse Voice Transcribe rejections

    A realtime stream rejected for exceeding a stream limit closes with 1013. A rejected file-transcription request returns HTTP 429 Too Many Requests. Transcription responses don't include the x-ratelimit-* headers.

    See also

    • Models: every model line, its versions, and where each one is available
    • Subscriptions: Muse Code plans, an alternative to pay-as-you-go
